simple: When you open the MicroProfiler, you see lots of strange labels like `stepHumanoid` or `computePath`. This page is a dictionary for those labels, called tags. For each one it says what Roblox is doing and how to make it faster. When you find a slow tag in your game, look it up here to know what to fix.
analogy: It is like the dashboard lights in a car. When a light turns on, you look it up in the manual to learn what it means and what to do about it.
keyPoints: Tags are also called tasks, timers, scopes, processes, or labels. Each one is a unit of work.
Sleep tags just mean a thread had nothing to do. Seeing lots of sleeping worker threads is normal.
Navigation tags like `computePath` come from pathfinding. Make fewer `Path:ComputeAsync()` calls and reuse paths for NPCs going to similar places.
Animation and humanoid tags like `stepHumanoid` and `stepAnimation` get faster with fewer Humanoids, fewer animated joints, and turning off states NPCs do not need, like Climbing or Swimming.
Networking tags grow when you replicate lots of objects, property changes, or events. Send fewer or smaller updates.
Rendering tags cover UI, particles, lighting, shadows, and transparency. Fewer visible parts, particles, lights, and see-through parts help.
Script tags like `Heartbeat/RunService.Heartbeat` and `GC` mean your code or the garbage collector is busy. Do less per frame and avoid making lots of temporary tables.
Simulation tags are physics. Fewer moving and colliding parts, simpler collision shapes, and not switching network ownership often all help.

terms.tag: A named chunk of work shown in the MicroProfiler, like `stepAnimation`.
terms.pathfinding: Finding a route for an NPC to walk from one spot to another around obstacles.
terms.tile: A small square section of the map that pathfinding uses. If a part in it moves, the tile has to be updated.
terms.Humanoid state: What a character is doing, like Running, Jumping, Climbing, or Swimming.
terms.replicate: Send changes from the server to players' devices, or the other way.
terms.packet: A small bundle of network data.
terms.streaming radius: How far around the player the game loads the world when streaming is on. Smaller radius means less data to send.
terms.adorn: An extra visual attached to an object, like a name tag or health bar above a character.
terms.frustum culling: Skipping drawing anything outside the camera's view, like objects behind you.
terms.shadow map: A picture the game makes to figure out where shadows fall. Not made at graphics quality below 4.
terms.post-processing: Effects added after the scene is drawn, like glow or color correction.
terms.garbage collection (GC): Luau automatically cleaning up memory from tables and values nothing uses anymore. Making lots of short-lived tables gives it more work.
terms.network ownership: Which computer, the server or a player's device, is in charge of a part's physics.
terms.assembly: A group of parts joined together that physics moves as one piece.
terms.simulation island: A group of parts that touch or connect to each other but not to other groups, so physics can handle each group on its own.
terms.throttled: Slowed down on purpose because there is too much work. When physics is throttled, only important things like Humanoids keep simulating.
terms.interpolate: Smoothly fill in movement between two known positions so objects do not jump.
terms.Z-order: The order UI elements are stacked from back to front.
terms.LayerCollector: A UI container like a `ScreenGui` or `BillboardGui` that holds other UI elements.

watchOut: Worrying about sleep tags. Sleeping threads are normal, not a problem.
Fixing a parent tag directly. Look at the slowest child tag under it first.
Moving lots of parts that pathfinding uses. Each move makes paths need to be recalculated.
Using partial transparency everywhere. Parts between 0.01 and 1 transparency take more rendering work than fully solid ones.
Doing heavy work right when input arrives or every Heartbeat. Do a small amount right away and spread bigger jobs over time.
